question: A team is designing an agent that must autonomously produce very long outputs, such as an extensive generated report or a large batch of generated code, and wants the model tier best associated with handling the most demanding, large-scale generation tasks. Which tier should they choose?
options: A) Any tier works equally well, since maximum output length does not differ meaningfully across current models
B) Claude Sonnet, since it is the only tier that supports generating long-form output at all
C) Claude Haiku, since its lower cost per token always outweighs output-length considerations for any task
D) Claude Opus, since it is positioned for the largest-scale, most complex generation and engineering tasks
correct_answers: D) Claude Opus, since it is positioned for the largest-scale, most complex generation and engineering tasks
explanations: Model tiers differ in intelligence, latency, and cost for demanding generation tasks, so the choice of tier is not interchangeable for the most complex, large-scale work described here.
Long-form output generation is supported across the current model lineup, not exclusively by Sonnet, so this option misstates the family's capabilities.
Lower cost per token is a real advantage of Haiku, but for the most demanding, large-scale generation tasks Anthropic points to the most capable tier rather than defaulting to the cheapest one.
Correct. Opus is recommended for the largest-scale, most complex engineering and generation work, matching a scenario centered on demanding, large-scale autonomous output generation.
